task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name (req_pipeline) and the request.pipeline action string are assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target request pipeline value is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The execute route selects its live request-transform configuration from a single click, capturing click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state.

The target path crosses delegated event handling, single-click action routing, the request gate, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling via Promise/setTimeout/MessageChannel, a window.postMessage relay, runtime slot materialization, request-transform conversion, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.

The same execute interaction produces non-target request.inspect/request.audit objects carrying req_pipeline-like values, plus request.pipeline objects carrying request_token/request_trace fields, before and around the target request.pipeline/req_pipeline object.
The deployed bundle also contains proof-like and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target req_pipeline field.
The target value is separated from the execute click by Promise.resolve, setTimeout, MessageChannel and window.postMessage boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the request transformer receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded request pipeline after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.subtype: route-selected additive-rotation Uint8Array-to-base64url request pipeline encoding
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is produced by materializing a runtime-dependent byte array via additive rotation accumulation through pipeline layers and encoding it as a stable rp_ request pipeline string. Triggered by a single button click (not two-stage). Uses MessageChannel and window.postMessage for main-thread async relay.

near_categories.why_not: The output is framed as a request pipeline token; the interaction is single-click; the relay uses postMessage/MessageChannel; the layer accumulation uses additive rotation.
The output has no cryptographic proof/token/seal semantics; proof-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
The target specifically constructs a request pipeline value via byte-array materialization rather than only formatting UI state.
The chain uses local DOM and form state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
